messages.content:
Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let all calculations be done modulo \(397\). Since \(397\) is prime, every nonzero residue has a multiplicative inverse.

If some \(a_k=0\), then the recurrence forces \(a_{k+1}=0\), and by induction \(a_{2026}=0\), contradicting \(a_{2026}=9\). Thus every \(a_n\) is invertible modulo \(397\).

Define

\[
x_n \equiv a_n^{-1} \pmod{397}.
\]

From

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397},
\]

we get

\[
a_{n+1} \equiv a_n(a_n+1)^{-2} \pmod{397}.
\]

Therefore

\[
x_{n+1}
\equiv \frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}
= a_n+2+\frac1{a_n}
= a_n+2+x_n \pmod{397}.
\]

So

\[
a_n \equiv x_{n+1}-x_n-2 \pmod{397}.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv x_{2027}-x_0-2(2027)
\pmod{397}.
\]

Now \(a_0=1\), so \(x_0=1\). Also \(a_{2026}=9\), so

\[
x_{2026}\equiv 9^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]

Since

\[
9\cdot 353 = 3177 \equiv 1 \pmod{397},
\]

we have \(x_{2026}=353\). Then

\[
x_{2027}\equiv x_{2026}+a_{2026}+2
=353+9+2
=364 \pmod{397}.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-4054 \pmod{397}.
\]

Since \(4054 \equiv 84 \pmod{397}\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-84
=279 \pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
